sanskrit: ānupūrvyeṇa vidhinā keśaveti punaḥ punaḥ sa cakṣuṣmān samabhavad gautamaś cābhavat punaḥ
english: By the prescribed rite, in due order, calling "Keśava" again and again, that Gautama regained his sight and became whole once more.

sanskrit: evaṃ hi varadaṃ nāma keśaveti mamārjuna devānām atha sarveṣām ṛṣīṇāṃ ca mahātmanām
english: Thus, O Arjuna, this name "Keśava" of mine is a boon-granting name to all the gods and to all the great-souled sages.

sanskrit: agniḥ somena saṃyukta ekayoni mukhaṃ kṛtam agnīṣomātmakaṃ tasmāj jagat kṛtsnaṃ carācaram
english: Agni joined with Soma was made a single womb, a single mouth; therefore this whole world, moving and unmoving, has the nature of Agni and Soma.

sanskrit: api hi purāṇe bhavati ekayonyātmakāv agnīṣomau devāś cāgnimukhā iti ekayonitvāc ca parasparaṃ mahayanto lokān dhārayata iti
english: And so it is said in the Purāṇa: Agni and Soma share one and the same womb, and the gods have Agni for their mouth; and because they share one womb, exalting each other, they uphold the worlds.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca agnīṣomau kathaṃ pūrvam ekayonī pravartitau eṣa me saṃśayo jātas taṃ chindhi madhusūdana
english: Arjuna said: How were Agni and Soma first brought forth from a single womb? This doubt has arisen in me; cut it away, O slayer of Madhu.

sanskrit: śrībhagavān uvāca hanta te vartayiṣyāmi purāṇaṃ pāṇḍunandana ātmatejodbhavaṃ pārtha śṛṇuṣvaikamanā mama
english: The Blessed Lord said: Come then, O son of Pāṇḍu, I shall relate to you an ancient tale, arisen from my own splendour; listen to me, O Pārtha, with single-minded attention.

sanskrit: saṃprakṣālanakāle 'tikrānte caturthe yugasahasrānte avyakte sarvabhūtapralaye sthāvarajaṅgame jyotirdharaṇivāyurahite 'ndhe tamasi jalaikārṇave loke tama ity evābhibhūte 'saṃjñake 'dvitīye pratiṣṭhite naiva rātryāṃ na divase na sati nāsati na vyakte nāvyakte vyavasthite etasyām avasthāyāṃ nārāyaṇaguṇāśrayād akṣayād ajarād anindriyād agrāhyād asaṃbhavāt satyād ahiṃsrāl lalāmād vividhapravṛttiviśeṣāt akṣayād ajarāmarād amūrtitaḥ sarvavyāpinaḥ sarvakartuḥ śāśvatāt tamasaḥ puruṣaḥ prādurbhūto harir avyayaḥ
english: When the time of the great dissolution had passed, at the end of the fourth thousand of the ages, when all beings, moving and unmoving, had merged into the Unmanifest, when light and earth and wind were no more, in blind darkness, the world a single ocean of water, overwhelmed by darkness alone, without consciousness, without a second, established—neither in night nor in day, neither in being nor in non-being, neither in the manifest nor in the unmanifest abiding—in this state, resting on the qualities of Nārāyaṇa, who is imperishable, ageless, beyond the senses, ungraspable, unborn, true, free from injury, the crest-jewel, the source of the manifold special activities, imperishable, ageless and deathless, formless, all-pervading, doer of all, eternal—from that darkness arose the Puruṣa, Hari the undecaying.

sanskrit: nidarśanam api hy atra bhavati nāsīd aho na rātrir āsīt na sad āsīn nāsad āsīt tama eva purastād abhavad viśvarūpam sā viśvasya jananīty evam asyārtho 'nubhāṣyate
english: And there is an illustration here: "There was no day, there was no night; there was no being, there was no non-being; darkness alone was there at first, having all forms—it was the mother of the universe." Thus is the meaning of this expounded.

sanskrit: tasyedānīṃ tamaḥsaṃbhavasya puruṣasya padmayoner brahmaṇaḥ prādurbhāve sa puruṣaḥ prajāḥ sisṛkṣamāṇo netrābhyām agnīṣomau sasarja tato bhūtasarge pravṛtte prajākramavaśād brahmakṣatram upātiṣṭhat yaḥ somas tad brahma yad brahma te brāhmaṇāḥ yo 'gnis tat kṣatraṃ kṣatrād brahma balavattaram kasmād iti lokapratyakṣaguṇam etat tad yathā brāhmaṇebhyaḥ paraṃ bhūtaṃ notpannapūrvam dīpyamāne 'gnau juhotīti kṛtvā bravīmi
english: Now of that Puruṣa born from the darkness—at the appearance of Brahmā, the lotus-born—that Puruṣa, desiring to create offspring, brought forth Agni and Soma from his two eyes. Then, when the creation of beings had begun, according to the order of progeny, the priestly and the warrior orders came into being: what is Soma, that is the Brahman; what is Brahman, those are the Brāhmaṇas; what is Agni, that is the Kṣatra. Yet the Brahman is mightier than the Kṣatra. Why? This is a quality plain to the world's sight, namely that no being higher than the Brāhmaṇas has ever arisen before; this I say, since it is into kindled fire that one offers oblation.

sanskrit: mantravādo 'pi hi bhavati tvam agne yajñānāṃ hotā viśveṣām hito devebhir mānuṣe jane iti nidarśanaṃ cātra bhavati viśveṣām agne yajñānāṃ hoteti hito devair mānuṣair jagata iti agnir hi yajñānāṃ hotā kartā
english: There is also the declaration of the mantra: "You, O Agni, are the hotṛ of all sacrifices, set among the race of men by the gods." And there is an illustration of this: "O Agni, you are the hotṛ of all sacrifices, set by the gods for men, for the world." For Agni is indeed the hotṛ, the performer of sacrifices.

sanskrit: na hy ṛte mantrād dhavanam asti na vinā puruṣaṃ tapaḥ saṃbhavati havir mantrāṇāṃ saṃpūjā vidyate devamanuṣyāṇām anena tvaṃ hoteti niyuktaḥ ye ca mānuṣā hotrādhikārās te ca brāhmaṇasya hi yājanaṃ vidhīyate na kṣatravaiśyayor dvijātyoḥ tasmād brāhmaṇā hy agnibhūtā yajñān udvahanti yajñā devāṃs tarpayanti devāḥ pṛthivīṃ bhāvayanti
english: For without the mantra there is no offering of oblation, and without a man no austerity comes about; the oblation is the honouring of the mantras of gods and men—by this you are appointed as hotṛ. And those human privileges of the hotṛ-office are ordained for the sacrificing of the Brāhmaṇa, not for the Kṣatriya and the Vaiśya, the twice-born. Therefore the Brāhmaṇas, having become Agni, bear up the sacrifices; the sacrifices satisfy the gods; and the gods foster the earth.

sanskrit: śatapathe hi brāhmaṇaṃ bhavati agnau samiddhe sa juhoti yo vidvān brāhmaṇamukhe dānāhutiṃ juhoti evam apy agnibhūtā brāhmaṇā vidvāṃso 'gniṃ bhāvayanti agnir viṣṇuḥ sarvabhūtāny anupraviśya prāṇān dhārayati api cātra sanatkumāragītāḥ ślokā bhavanti
english: For in the Śatapatha there is a Brāhmaṇa text: "It is into kindled fire that he offers, the learned one who offers the oblation of the gift into the mouth of a Brāhmaṇa." Thus too, the learned Brāhmaṇas, having become Agni, foster the fire. Agni is Viṣṇu; entering into all beings, he sustains their vital breaths. And here too there are verses sung by Sanatkumāra:

sanskrit: viśvaṃ brahmāsṛjat pūrvaṃ sarvādir niravaskaram brahmaghoṣair divaṃ tiṣṭhanty amarā brahmayonayaḥ
english: In the beginning Brahmā created the universe, the source of all, free of impurity; by the chants of the Brahman the immortals, born of the Brahman, abide in heaven.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇānāṃ matir vākyaṃ karma śraddhā tapāṃsi ca dhārayanti mahīṃ dyāṃ ca śaityād vāry amṛtaṃ yathā
english: The thought, the speech, the rites, the faith, and the austerities of the Brāhmaṇas uphold the earth and the sky, as the cool water sustains by its coolness, like nectar.

sanskrit: nāsti satyāt paro dharmo nāsti mātṛsamo guruḥ brāhmaṇebhyaḥ paraṃ nāsti pretya ceha ca bhūtaye
english: There is no dharma higher than truth; there is no teacher equal to a mother; there is nothing higher than the Brāhmaṇas for one's welfare, here and in the world to come.

sanskrit: naiṣām ukṣā vardhate nota vāhā; na gargaro mathyate saṃpradāne apadhvastā dasyubhūtā bhavanti; yeṣāṃ rāṣṭre brāhmaṇā vṛttihīnāḥ
english: For them no bull thrives, nor any draught-ox; no churn is plied at the sacrificial offering. Cast down, turned to barbarians, do those become in whose kingdom the Brāhmaṇas are bereft of their livelihood.

sanskrit: vedapurāṇetihāsaprāmāṇyān nārāyaṇamukhodgatāḥ sarvātmānaḥ sarvakartāraḥ sarvabhāvanāś ca brāhmaṇāḥ vāksamakālaṃ hi tasya devasya varapradasya brāhmaṇāḥ prathamaṃ prādurbhūtā brāhmaṇebhyaś ca śeṣā varṇāḥ prādurbhūtāḥ itthaṃ ca surāsuraviśiṣṭā brāhmaṇā yadā mayā brahmabhūtena purā svayam evotpāditāḥ surāsuramaharṣayo bhūtaviśeṣāḥ sthāpitā nigṛhītāś ca
english: On the authority of the Vedas, the Purāṇas, and the histories, the Brāhmaṇas—issued from the mouth of Nārāyaṇa, having all for their self, doing all, fostering all—the Brāhmaṇas came forth first, simultaneously with the speech of that boon-granting god; and from the Brāhmaṇas the remaining castes came forth. Thus the Brāhmaṇas, distinguished above gods and demons, when of old by me, having become the Brahman, they were myself produced, then the gods, the demons, and the great sages, those distinct kinds of beings, were established and held in check.

sanskrit: ahalyādharṣaṇanimittaṃ hi gautamād dhariśmaśrutām indraḥ prāptaḥ kauśikanimittaṃ cendro muṣkaviyogaṃ meṣavṛṣaṇatvaṃ cāvāpa aśvinor grahapratiṣedhodyatavajrasya puraṃdarasya cyavanena stambhito bāhuḥ kratuvadhaprāptamanyunā ca dakṣeṇa bhūyas tapasā cātmānaṃ saṃyojya netrākṛtir anyā lalāṭe rudrasyotpāditā
english: For on account of the violation of Ahalyā, Indra received from Gautama a green-tinged beard; and on the Kauśika's account Indra suffered the loss of his testicles and obtained those of a ram. When Purandara had raised his thunderbolt to forbid the libation to the Aśvins, his arm was made rigid by Cyavana. And by Dakṣa, wrathful at the destruction of his sacrifice, having again joined himself to austerity, another eye in the shape of an eye was produced on the forehead of Rudra.

sanskrit: tripuravadhārthaṃ dīkṣām abhyupagatasya rudrasyośanasā śiraso jaṭā utkṛtya prayuktāḥ tataḥ prādurbhūtā bhujagāḥ tair asya bhujagaiḥ pīḍyamānaḥ kaṇṭho nīlatām upanītaḥ pūrve ca manvantare svāyaṃbhuve nārāyaṇahastabandhagrahaṇān nīlakaṇṭhatvam eva vā
english: When Rudra had undertaken the consecration for the slaying of Tripura, Uśanas tore the matted locks from his head and cast them down; from them serpents came forth. Tormented by those serpents, his throat was brought to a dark-blue hue. Or else his blue-throatedness came in the former age of Manu Svāyaṃbhuva, from the grip of Nārāyaṇa's binding hand.

sanskrit: amṛtotpādane puraścaraṇatām upagatasyāṅgiraso bṛhaspater upaspṛśato na prasādaṃ gatavatyaḥ kilāpaḥ atha bṛhaspatir apāṃ cukrodha yasmān mamopaspṛśataḥ kaluṣībhūtā na prasādam upagatās tasmād adyaprabhṛti jhaṣamakaramatsyakacchapajantusaṃkīrṇāḥ kaluṣībhavateti tadāprabhṛty āpo yādobhiḥ saṃkīrṇāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ
english: At the churning out of the nectar, when Bṛhaspati of the line of Aṅgiras, undertaking the preliminary rite, touched the waters, they did not, it is said, become clear. Then Bṛhaspati grew angry at the waters: "Since, when I touch you, you grow turbid and do not become clear, therefore from this day onward become turbid, teeming with great fish, makaras, fish, tortoises, and creatures." From that day onward the waters became filled with aquatic beasts.

sanskrit: viśvarūpo vai tvāṣṭraḥ purohito devānām āsīt svasrīyo 'surāṇām sa pratyakṣaṃ devebhyo bhāgam adadat parokṣam asurebhyaḥ
english: Viśvarūpa, son of Tvaṣṭṛ, was the chaplain of the gods and the sister's son of the demons. Openly he gave the sacrificial portion to the gods, but secretly to the demons.

sanskrit: atha hiraṇyakaśipuṃ puraskṛtya viśvarūpamātaraṃ svasāram asurā varam ayācanta he svasar ayaṃ te putras tvāṣṭro viśvarūpas triśirā devānāṃ purohitaḥ pratyakṣaṃ devebhyo bhāgam adadat parokṣam asmākam tato devā vardhante vayaṃ kṣīyāmaḥ tad enaṃ tvaṃ vārayitum arhasi tathā yathāsmān bhajed iti
english: Then, putting Hiraṇyakaśipu at their head, the demons begged a boon of their sister, the mother of Viśvarūpa: "O sister, this son of yours, Viśvarūpa the three-headed, son of Tvaṣṭṛ, the chaplain of the gods, openly gives the portion to the gods but secretly to us. Thereby the gods wax strong and we wane. You ought therefore to restrain him, so that he may favour us."

sanskrit: atha viśvarūpaṃ nandanavanam upagataṃ mātovāca putra kiṃ parapakṣavardhanas tvaṃ mātulapakṣaṃ nāśayasi nārhasy evaṃ kartum iti sa viśvarūpo mātur vākyam anatikramaṇīyam iti matvā saṃpūjya hiraṇyakaśipum agāt
english: Then, when Viśvarūpa had come to the Nandana grove, his mother said to him: "My son, why do you, a fosterer of the other side, work the ruin of your maternal uncles' party? You ought not to do thus." And Viśvarūpa, deeming his mother's word not to be transgressed, did honour to Hiraṇyakaśipu and went over to him.

sanskrit: hairaṇyagarbhāc ca vasiṣṭhād dhiraṇyakaśipuḥ śāpaṃ prāptavān yasmāt tvayānyo vṛto hotā tasmād asamāptayajñas tvam apūrvāt sattvajātād vadhaṃ prāpsyasīti tacchāpadānād dhiraṇyakaśipuḥ prāptavān vadham
english: And from Vasiṣṭha, born of Hiraṇyagarbha, Hiraṇyakaśipu received a curse: "Since another was chosen by you as hotṛ, therefore, with your sacrifice left unfinished, you shall meet your death from a kind of being never seen before." By the giving of that curse Hiraṇyakaśipu met his death.

sanskrit: viśvarūpo mātṛpakṣavardhano 'tyarthaṃ tapasy abhavat tasya vratabhaṅgārtham indro bahvīḥ śrīmatyo 'psaraso niyuyoja tāś ca dṛṣṭvā manaḥ kṣubhitaṃ tasyābhavat tāsu cāpsaraḥsu nacirād eva sakto 'bhavat saktaṃ cainaṃ jñātvāpsarasa ūcur gacchāmahe vayaṃ yathāgatam iti
english: Viśvarūpa, fosterer of his mother's side, gave himself exceedingly to austerity. To break his vow Indra dispatched many lovely apsarases; and at the sight of them his mind grew troubled, and before long he became attached to those apsarases. Knowing him attached, the apsarases said: "We are going, back the way we came."

sanskrit: tās tvāṣṭra uvāca kva gamiṣyatha āsyatāṃ tāvan mayā saha śreyo bhaviṣyatīti tās tam abruvan vayaṃ devastriyo 'psarasa indraṃ varadaṃ purā prabhaviṣṇuṃ vṛṇīmaha iti
english: To them the son of Tvaṣṭṛ said: "Where will you go? Stay awhile here with me; it will be for your good." They said to him: "We are women of the gods, apsarases; long ago we chose Indra, the boon-giver, the mighty, as our lord."

sanskrit: atha tā viśvarūpo 'bravīd adyaiva sendrā devā na bhaviṣyantīti tato mantrāñ jajāpa tair mantraiḥ prāvardhata triśirāḥ ekenāsyena sarvalokeṣu dvijaiḥ kriyāvadbhir yajñeṣu suhutaṃ somaṃ papāv ekenāpa ekena sendrān devān athendras taṃ vivardhamānaṃ somapānāpyāyitasarvagātraṃ dṛṣṭvā cintām āpede
english: Then Viśvarūpa said to them: "This very day the gods, with Indra, shall be no more." Then he muttered his mantras, and by those mantras the three-headed one grew great. With one mouth he drank the soma well offered in the sacrifices of ritual-performing twice-born throughout all the worlds; with another he drank the waters; with another he would swallow the gods together with Indra. Then Indra, seeing him swelling, all his limbs nourished by the drinking of soma, fell into anxious thought.

sanskrit: devāś ca te sahendreṇa brahmāṇam abhijagmur ūcuś ca viśvarūpeṇa sarvayajñeṣu suhutaḥ somaḥ pīyate vayam abhāgāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ asurapakṣo vardhate vayaṃ kṣīyāmaḥ tad arhasi no vidhātuṃ śreyo yad anantaram iti
english: And those gods, together with Indra, went to Brahmā and said: "By Viśvarūpa the soma well offered in all sacrifices is being drunk; we are left without our portion. The demons' party waxes; we wane. You ought therefore to ordain for us whatever good may follow."

sanskrit: tān brahmovāca ṛṣir bhārgavas tapas tapyate dadhīcaḥ sa yācyatāṃ varaṃ yathā kalevaraṃ jahyāt tasyāsthibhir vajraṃ kriyatām iti
english: To them Brahmā said: "The sage Dadhīca of Bhṛgu's line is performing austerities. Let him be entreated for a boon, that he may give up his body; from his bones let the thunderbolt be made."

sanskrit: devās tatrāgacchan yatra dadhīco bhagavān ṛṣis tapas tepe sendrā devās tam abhigamyocur bhagavaṃs tapasaḥ kuśalam avighnaṃ ceti tān dadhīca uvāca svāgataṃ bhavadbhyaḥ kiṃ kriyatām yad vakṣyatha tat kariṣyāmīti te tam abruvañ śarīraparityāgaṃ lokahitārthaṃ bhagavān kartum arhatīti atha dadhīcas tathaivāvimanāḥ sukhaduḥkhasamo mahāyogī ātmānaṃ samādhāya śarīraparityāgaṃ cakāra
english: The gods went there, where the blessed sage Dadhīca performed his austerities. The gods, with Indra, approached him and said: "O blessed one, is your austerity faring well and without hindrance?" To them Dadhīca said: "Welcome to you. What shall be done? Whatever you shall say, that I will do." They said to him: "For the good of the worlds the blessed one ought to give up his body." Then Dadhīca, untroubled even at this, even-minded in pleasure and pain, the great yogin, collecting himself, made the abandonment of his body.

sanskrit: tasya paramātmany avasṛte tāny asthīni dhātā saṃgṛhya vajram akarot tena vajreṇābhedyenāpradhṛṣyeṇa brahmāsthisaṃbhūtena viṣṇupraviṣṭenendro viśvarūpaṃ jaghāna śirasāṃ cāsya chedanam akarot tasmād anantaraṃ viśvarūpagātramathanasaṃbhavaṃ tvaṣṭrotpāditam evāriṃ vṛtram indro jaghāna
english: When his soul had departed into the Supreme Self, the Ordainer took up those bones and made the thunderbolt. With that thunderbolt, unbreakable and unassailable, born of a Brāhmaṇa's bones and entered by Viṣṇu, Indra slew Viśvarūpa and severed his heads. Thereafter Indra slew the foe Vṛtra, arisen from the churning of Viśvarūpa's body and produced by Tvaṣṭṛ.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ dvaidhībhūtāyāṃ brahmavadhyāyāṃ bhayād indro devarājyaṃ parityajya apsu saṃbhavāṃ śītalāṃ mānasasarogatāṃ nalinīṃ prapede tatra caiśvaryayogād aṇumātro bhūtvā bisagranthiṃ praviveśa
english: When that guilt of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter had become twofold, Indra, out of fear, abandoned the kingship of the gods and took refuge in a cool lotus growing in the waters, in Lake Mānasa; and there, by the power of his lordly might, becoming no larger than an atom, he entered into the fibre of a lotus-stalk.

sanskrit: atha brahmavadhyābhayapranaṣṭe trailokyanāthe śacīpatau jagad anīśvaraṃ babhūva devān rajas tamaś cāviveśa mantrā na prāvartanta maharṣīṇām rakṣāṃsi prādurabhavan brahma cotsādanaṃ jagāma anindrāś cābalā lokāḥ supradhṛṣyā babhūvuḥ
english: Then, when the lord of the three worlds, the husband of Śacī, had vanished out of fear of the Brāhmaṇa-slaughter, the world became without a ruler. Passion and darkness entered the gods; the mantras of the great sages no longer availed; the rākṣasas came forth; the Brahman went to ruin; and the worlds, without Indra and powerless, became easy prey.

sanskrit: atha devā ṛṣayaś cāyuṣaḥ putraṃ nahuṣaṃ nāma devarājatve 'bhiṣiṣicuḥ nahuṣaḥ pañcabhiḥ śatair jyotiṣāṃ lalāṭe jvaladbhiḥ sarvatejoharais triviṣṭapaṃ pālayāṃ babhūva atha lokāḥ prakṛtim āpedire svasthāś ca babhūvuḥ
english: Then the gods and the sages consecrated to the kingship of the gods the son of Āyus, Nahuṣa by name. Nahuṣa, with five hundred blazing luminaries on his forehead that stole away all splendour, governed the heaven; and the worlds returned to their natural state and grew at ease.

sanskrit: athovāca nahuṣaḥ sarvaṃ māṃ śakropabhuktam upasthitam ṛte śacīm iti sa evam uktvā śacīsamīpam agamad uvāca cainām subhage 'ham indro devānāṃ bhajasva mām iti taṃ śacī pratyuvāca prakṛtyā tvaṃ dharmavatsalaḥ somavaṃśodbhavaś ca nārhasi parapatnīdharṣaṇaṃ kartum iti
english: Then Nahuṣa said: "All that was enjoyed by Śakra has come to me, save Śacī alone." Having said this, he went near to Śacī and said to her: "O fair one, I am the Indra of the gods; give yourself to me." Śacī answered him: "By nature you are devoted to dharma and sprung from the lineage of Soma; you ought not to do violence to another's wife."

sanskrit: tām athovāca nahuṣaḥ aindraṃ padam adhyāsyate mayā aham indrasya rājyaratnaharo nātrādharmaḥ kaś cit tvam indrabhukteti sā tam uvāca asti mama kiṃ cid vratam aparyavasitam tasyāvabhṛthe tvām upagamiṣyāmi kaiś cid evāhobhir iti sa śacyaivam abhihito nahuṣo jagāma
english: Then Nahuṣa said to her: "The seat of Indra is occupied by me; I am the bearer-off of Indra's royal treasures; there is no unrighteousness in this—you were Indra's enjoyment." She said to him: "I have a certain vow not yet completed. At its concluding bath I shall come to you, in but a few days." Thus addressed by Śacī, Nahuṣa went away.

sanskrit: atha śacī duḥkhaśokārtā bhartṛdarśanalālasā nahuṣabhayagṛhītā bṛhaspatim upāgacchat sa ca tām abhigatāṃ dṛṣṭvaiva dhyānaṃ praviśya bhartṛkāryatatparāṃ jñātvā bṛhaspatir uvāca anenaiva vratena tapasā cānvitā devīṃ varadām upaśrutim āhvaya sā tavendraṃ darśayiṣyatīti
english: Then Śacī, afflicted with grief and sorrow, longing for the sight of her husband, seized with fear of Nahuṣa, went to Bṛhaspati. And he, the moment he saw her come, entered into meditation, and knowing her intent upon her husband's cause, Bṛhaspati said: "Endowed with this very vow and austerity, summon the boon-granting goddess Upaśruti; she will show you Indra."

sanskrit: sātha mahāniyamam āsthitā devīṃ varadām upaśrutiṃ mantrair āhvayat sopaśrutiḥ śacīsamīpam agāt uvāca cainām iyam asmi tvayopahūtopasthitā kiṃ te priyaṃ karavāṇīti tāṃ mūrdhnā praṇamyovāca śacī bhagavaty arhasi me bhartāraṃ darśayituṃ tvaṃ satyā matā ceti saināṃ mānasaṃ saro 'nayat tatrendraṃ bisagranthigatam adarśayat
english: Then she, undertaking a great observance, summoned by mantras the boon-granting goddess Upaśruti. That Upaśruti came near to Śacī and said to her: "Here I am, summoned by you and present. What dear thing shall I do for you?" Bowing to her with her head, Śacī said: "O blessed lady, you ought to show me my husband; you are held to be true." Then Upaśruti led her to Lake Mānasa and showed her Indra, gone into the fibre of a lotus-stalk.

sanskrit: tām indraḥ patnīṃ kṛśāṃ glānāṃ ca dṛṣṭvā cintayāṃ babhūva aho mama mahad duḥkham idam adyopagatam naṣṭaṃ hi mām iyam anviṣyopāgamad duḥkhārteti tām indra uvāca kathaṃ vartayasīti sā tam uvāca nahuṣo mām āhvayati kālaś cāsya mayā kṛta iti
english: Indra, seeing his wife wasted and worn, fell to thinking: "Alas, this great grief has now come upon me, that she, afflicted with sorrow, has come seeking me out who was lost." Indra said to her: "How do you fare?" She said to him: "Nahuṣa summons me, and a time has been appointed by me for him."

sanskrit: tām indra uvāca gaccha nahuṣas tvayā vācyo 'pūrveṇa mām ṛṣiyuktena yānena tvam adhirūḍha udvahasva indrasya hi mahānti vāhanāni manasaḥ priyāṇy adhirūḍhāni mayā tvam anyenopayātum arhasīti saivam uktā hṛṣṭā jagāma indro 'pi bisagranthim evāviveśa bhūyaḥ
english: Indra said to her: "Go, and say this to Nahuṣa: 'Mount and bear me away in a wondrous, unheard-of car yoked with sages; for Indra has great vehicles, the heart's delight, which I have mounted. You ought to come to me by some other means.'" Thus addressed, she went gladly; and Indra entered once more into the fibre of the lotus-stalk.

sanskrit: athendrāṇīm abhyāgatāṃ dṛṣṭvovāca nahuṣaḥ pūrṇaḥ sa kāla iti taṃ śacy abravīc chakreṇa yathoktam sa maharṣiyuktaṃ vāhanam adhirūḍhaḥ śacīsamīpam upāgacchat
english: Then, seeing Indra's consort approach, Nahuṣa said: "That time is fulfilled." Śacī told him what Śakra had said; and mounting a vehicle yoked with great sages, he came near to Śacī.

sanskrit: atha maitrāvaruṇiḥ kumbhayonir agastyo maharṣīn vikriyamāṇāṃs tān nahuṣeṇāpaśyat padbhyāṃ ca tenāspṛśyata tataḥ sa nahuṣam abravīd akāryapravṛtta pāpa patasva mahīm sarpo bhava yāvad bhūmir girayaś ca tiṣṭheyus tāvad iti sa maharṣivākyasamakālam eva tasmād yānād avāpatat
english: Then Agastya, son of Mitra and Varuṇa, the pitcher-born, saw those great sages being maltreated by Nahuṣa, and was touched by his feet; whereupon he said to Nahuṣa: "Set upon a deed undone, O sinner, fall to the earth; become a serpent, and so remain for as long as the earth and mountains shall stand." And at the very moment of the great sage's word, he fell down from that car.

sanskrit: athānindraṃ punas trailokyam abhavat tato devā ṛṣayaś ca bhagavantaṃ viṣṇuṃ śaraṇam indrārthe 'bhijagmuḥ ūcuś cainaṃ bhagavann indraṃ brahmavadhyābhibhūtaṃ trātum arhasīti tataḥ sa varadas tān abravīd aśvamedhaṃ yajñaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ śakro 'bhiyajatu tataḥ svaṃ sthānaṃ prāpsyatīti
english: Then the three worlds were again without an Indra. Thereupon the gods and the sages went for refuge to the blessed Viṣṇu for Indra's sake and said to him: "O blessed one, you ought to deliver Indra, overwhelmed by the guilt of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter." Then that boon-giver said to them: "Let Śakra offer the horse-sacrifice, the Vaiṣṇava rite; thereby he shall regain his own station."

sanskrit: tato devā ṛṣayaś cendraṃ nāpaśyan yadā tadā śacīm ūcur gaccha subhage indram ānayasveti sā punas tat saraḥ samabhyagacchat indraś ca tasmāt sarasaḥ samutthāya bṛhaspatim abhijagāma bṛhaspatiś cāśvamedhaṃ mahākratuṃ śakrāyāharat tataḥ kṛṣṇasāraṅgaṃ medhyam aśvam utsṛjya vāhanaṃ tam eva kṛtvā indraṃ marutpatiṃ bṛhaspatiḥ svasthānaṃ prāpayām āsa
english: Then, when the gods and the sages did not see Indra, they said to Śacī: "Go, O fair one, and fetch Indra." She again went to that lake, and Indra, rising up out of that lake, went to Bṛhaspati. And Bṛhaspati performed the horse-sacrifice, the great rite, for Śakra; then, releasing a dappled black horse fit for sacrifice and making that his vehicle, Bṛhaspati restored Indra, the lord of the Maruts, to his own station.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa devarāḍ devair ṛṣibhiḥ stūyamānas triviṣṭapastho niṣkalmaṣo babhūva brahmavadhyāṃ caturṣu sthāneṣu vanitāgnivanaspatigoṣu vyabhajat evam indro brahmatejaḥprabhāvopabṛṃhitaḥ śatruvadhaṃ kṛtvā svasthānaṃ prāpitaḥ
english: Then that king of the gods, praised by gods and sages, abiding in heaven, became free of stain; he distributed the guilt of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter among four receptacles—women, fire, trees, and cattle. Thus Indra, strengthened by the might and splendour of the Brahman, having slain his foe, was restored to his own station.

sanskrit: ākāśagaṅgāgataś ca purā bharadvājo maharṣir upāspṛśaṃs trīn kramān kramatā viṣṇunābhyāsāditaḥ sa bharadvājena sasalilena pāṇinorasi tāḍitaḥ salakṣaṇoraskaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ
english: And of old the great sage Bharadvāja, having come to the celestial Gaṅgā and touching its water, was approached by Viṣṇu as he strode his three steps; he was struck on the chest by Bharadvāja with a water-filled hand, and so came to bear that mark upon his breast.

sanskrit: bhṛguṇā maharṣiṇā śapto 'gniḥ sarvabhakṣatvam upanītaḥ
english: Cursed by the great sage Bhṛgu, Agni was reduced to the state of devourer of all things.

sanskrit: aditir vai devānām annam apacad etad bhuktvāsurān haniṣyantīti tatra budho vratacaryāsamāptāv āgacchat aditiṃ cāvocad bhikṣāṃ dehīti tatra devaiḥ pūrvam etat prāśyaṃ nānyenety aditir bhikṣāṃ nādāt atha bhikṣāpratyākhyānaruṣitena budhena brahmabhūtena vivasvato dvitīye janmany aṇḍasaṃjñitasyāṇḍaṃ māritam adityāḥ sa mārtaṇḍo vivasvān abhavac chrāddhadevaḥ
english: Aditi cooked food for the gods, thinking, "Having eaten this, they shall slay the demons." There came Budha at the completion of his observance and said to Aditi: "Give me alms." But "this is to be eaten first by the gods, by no other," thought Aditi, and gave no alms. Then Budha, enraged at the refusal of alms, having become the Brahman, killed the egg of Aditi—the egg-named one at the second birth of Vivasvān; that dead egg became Vivasvān, the Mārtaṇḍa, the god of the funeral offerings.

sanskrit: dakṣasya vai duhitaraḥ ṣaṣṭir āsan tābhyaḥ kaśyapāya trayodaśa prādād daśa dharmāya daśa manave saptaviṃśatim indave tāsu tulyāsu nakṣatrākhyāṃ gatāsu somo rohiṇyām abhyadhikāṃ prītim akarot tatas tāḥ śeṣāḥ patnya īrṣyāvatyaḥ pituḥ samīpaṃ gatvemam arthaṃ śaśaṃsuḥ bhagavann asmāsu tulyaprabhāvāsu somo rohiṇīm adhikaṃ bhajatīti so 'bravīd yakṣmainam āvekṣyatīti
english: Dakṣa had sixty daughters; of them he gave thirteen to Kaśyapa, ten to Dharma, ten to Manu, and twenty-seven to the Moon. Though all these were equal and bore the names of the lunar mansions, Soma showed excessive affection to Rohiṇī. Then the rest of his wives, grown jealous, went to their father and told him this matter: "O blessed one, though we are of equal worth, Soma favours Rohiṇī above us." He said: "Consumption shall enter him."

sanskrit: dakṣaśāpāt somaṃ rājānaṃ yakṣmāviveśa sa yakṣmaṇāviṣṭo dakṣam agamat dakṣaś cainam abravīn na samaṃ vartasa iti tatrarṣayaḥ somam abruvan kṣīyase yakṣmaṇā paścimasyāṃ diśi samudre hiraṇyasarastīrtham tatra gatvātmānam abhiṣecayasveti athāgacchat somas tatra hiraṇyasarastīrtham
english: By Dakṣa's curse consumption entered King Soma; and seized by consumption he went to Dakṣa. Dakṣa said to him: "You do not deal evenly." Thereupon the sages said to Soma: "You are wasting away with consumption. In the western quarter, in the ocean, is the holy ford of the Golden Lake; go there and bathe yourself." Then Soma went there, to the holy ford of the Golden Lake.

sanskrit: sthūlaśirā maharṣir meroḥ prāguttare digbhāge tapas tepe tasya tapas tapyamānasya sarvagandhavahaḥ śucir vāyur vivāyamānaḥ śarīram aspṛśat sa tapasā tāpitaśarīraḥ kṛśo vāyunopavījyamāno hṛdayaparitoṣam agamat tatra tasyānilavyajanakṛtaparitoṣasya sadyo vanaspatayaḥ puṣpaśobhāṃ na darśitavanta iti sa etāñ śaśāpa na sarvakālaṃ puṣpavanto bhaviṣyatheti
english: The great sage Sthūlaśiras performed austerities in the north-eastern region of Meru. As he performed his austerity, a pure breeze, bearing all fragrances and blowing gently, touched his body. With his body heated and wasted by austerity, fanned by the wind, he came to gladness of heart. But there, while he took delight in the wind's fanning, the trees did not at once display the beauty of their blossoms; so he cursed them: "You shall not bear flowers at all seasons."

sanskrit: nārāyaṇo lokahitārthaṃ vaḍavāmukho nāma maharṣiḥ purābhavat tasya merau tapas tapyataḥ samudra āhūto nāgataḥ tenāmarṣitenātmagātroṣmaṇā samudraḥ stimitajalaḥ kṛtaḥ svedaprasyandanasadṛśaś cāsya lavaṇabhāvo janitaḥ uktaś cāpeyo bhaviṣyasi etac ca te toyaṃ vaḍavāmukhasaṃjñitena pīyamānaṃ madhuraṃ bhaviṣyati tad etad adyāpi vaḍavāmukhasaṃjñitenānuvartinā toyaṃ sāmudraṃ pīyate
english: Of old Nārāyaṇa, for the good of the worlds, became a great sage named Vaḍavāmukha. As he performed his austerities on Meru, the ocean, when summoned, did not come. Enraged thereby, by the heat of his own body he made the ocean's waters still, and brought into being its salt nature, like the trickling of sweat. And he said: "You shall become undrinkable, and this water of yours, when drunk by one bearing the name Vaḍavāmukha, shall become sweet." So even to this day the ocean's water is drunk by him called Vaḍavāmukha, ever continuing.

sanskrit: himavato girer duhitaram umāṃ rudraś cakame bhṛgur api ca maharṣir himavantam āgamyābravīt kanyām umāṃ me dehīti tam abravīd dhimavān abhilaṣito varo rudra iti tam abravīd bhṛgur yasmāt tvayāhaṃ kanyāvaraṇakṛtabhāvaḥ pratyākhyātas tasmān na ratnānāṃ bhavān bhājanaṃ bhaviṣyatīti adyaprabhṛty etad avasthitam ṛṣivacanam
english: Rudra loved Umā, daughter of the mountain Himavat. The great sage Bhṛgu too came to Himavat and said: "Give me the maiden Umā." Himavat said to him: "Rudra is the suitor desired." Bhṛgu said to him: "Since I, intent on choosing the maiden, have been refused by you, therefore you shall not be a receptacle of jewels." From that day onward this word of the sage has held firm.

sanskrit: tad evaṃvidhaṃ māhātmyaṃ brāhmaṇānām kṣatram api śāśvatīm avyayāṃ pṛthivīṃ patnīm abhigamya bubhuje tad etad brahmāgnīṣomīyam tena jagad dhāryate
english: Such is the greatness of the Brāhmaṇas. The Kṣatra too, having wedded the everlasting, imperishable Earth as its wife, enjoyed her. This is the Brahman, born of Agni and Soma; by it the world is upheld.

sanskrit: śrībhagavān uvāca sūryācandramasau śaśvat keśair me aṃśusaṃjñitaiḥ bodhayaṃs tāpayaṃś caiva jagad uttiṣṭhataḥ pṛthak
english: The Blessed Lord said: The sun and the moon, ever with my rays that are called my hair, awakening and warming the world, rise up severally.

sanskrit: bodhanāt tāpanāc caiva jagato harṣaṇaṃ bhavet agnīṣomakṛtair ebhiḥ karmabhiḥ pāṇḍunandana hṛṣīkeśo 'ham īśāno varado lokabhāvanaḥ
english: By this awakening and warming the gladdening of the world comes about; by these deeds wrought of Agni and Soma, O son of Pāṇḍu, I am Hṛṣīkeśa, the lord, the boon-giver, the fosterer of the worlds.

sanskrit: iḍopahūtayogena hare bhāgaṃ kratuṣv aham varṇaś ca me hariśreṣṭhas tasmād dharir ahaṃ smṛtaḥ
english: Through the summoning of the iḍā-offering I take, O tawny one, my portion in the sacrifices; and my colour is the finest tawny-green; therefore am I remembered as Hari.

sanskrit: dhāma sāro hi lokānām ṛtaṃ caiva vicāritam ṛtadhāmā tato vipraiḥ satyaś cāhaṃ prakīrtitaḥ
english: My abode is the essence of the worlds, and the cosmic order has been discerned; therefore by the wise I am proclaimed Ṛtadhāman, abode of order, and the True.

sanskrit: naṣṭāṃ ca dharaṇīṃ pūrvam avindaṃ vai guhāgatām govinda iti māṃ devā vāgbhiḥ samabhituṣṭuvuḥ
english: And of old I recovered the lost earth that had gone into the cavern; therefore the gods extolled me with their voices as Govinda.

sanskrit: śipiviṣṭeti cākhyāyāṃ hīnaromā ca yo bhavet tenāviṣṭaṃ hi yat kiṃ cic chipiviṣṭaṃ hi tat smṛtam
english: And in the name "Śipiviṣṭa": he who is without hair, and whatever is pervaded by him—that is remembered as śipiviṣṭa.

sanskrit: yāsko mām ṛṣir avyagro naikayajñeṣu gītavān śipiviṣṭa iti hy asmād guhyanāmadharo hy aham
english: The sage Yāska, untroubled, sang of me in many sacrifices as Śipiviṣṭa; therefore I bear this hidden name.

sanskrit: stutvā māṃ śipiviṣṭeti yāsko ṛṣir udāradhīḥ matprasādād adho naṣṭaṃ niruktam abhijagmivān
english: Having praised me as Śipiviṣṭa, the sage Yāska of noble mind, by my grace, recovered the lost etymology that had fallen away.

sanskrit: na hi jāto na jāye 'haṃ na janiṣye kadā cana kṣetrajñaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ tasmād aham ajaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: I have not been born, I am not born, nor shall I ever be born; I am the Knower of the Field in all beings; therefore am I remembered as the Unborn.

sanskrit: noktapūrvaṃ mayā kṣudram aślīlaṃ vā kadā cana ṛtā brahmasutā sā me satyā devī sarasvatī
english: Never before have I uttered anything mean or unseemly; true is that goddess Sarasvatī, daughter of the Brahman, true and unfailing, who is mine.

sanskrit: sac cāsac caiva kaunteya mayāveśitam ātmani pauṣkare brahmasadane satyaṃ mām ṛṣayo viduḥ
english: Both being and non-being, O son of Kuntī, have been set by me within myself; in the lotus-seat, the abode of the Brahman, the sages know me as the True.

sanskrit: sattvān na cyutapūrvo 'haṃ sattvaṃ vai viddhi matkṛtam janmanīhābhavat sattvaṃ paurvikaṃ me dhanaṃjaya
english: Never before have I fallen from goodness; know that goodness is wrought by me; in this birth the goodness that became mine was of an earlier time, O Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: nirāśīḥkarmasaṃyuktaṃ sātvataṃ māṃ prakalpaya sātvatajñānadṛṣṭo 'haṃ sātvataḥ sātvatāṃ patiḥ
english: Conceive of me as the Sātvata, joined to action without desire for reward; seen through the knowledge of the Sātvatas, I am the Sātvata, the lord of the Sātvatas.

sanskrit: kṛṣāmi medinīṃ pārtha bhūtvā kārṣṇāyaso mahān kṛṣṇo varṇaś ca me yasmāt tasmāt kṛṣṇo 'ham arjuna
english: I plough the earth, O Pārtha, becoming the great ploughshare of black iron; and since my colour is dark, therefore am I Kṛṣṇa, O Arjuna.

sanskrit: mayā saṃśleṣitā bhūmir adbhir vyoma ca vāyunā vāyuś ca tejasā sārdhaṃ vaikuṇṭhatvaṃ tato mama
english: By me the earth has been joined with the waters, and the sky with the wind, and the wind together with fire; thence comes my state of Vaikuṇṭha, the unhindered.

sanskrit: nirvāṇaṃ paramaṃ saukhyaṃ dharmo 'sau para ucyate tasmān na cyutapūrvo 'ham acyutas tena karmaṇā
english: Nirvāṇa is the supreme bliss; that is called the highest dharma; and since I have never before fallen from it, by that deed I am Acyuta, the Unfallen.

sanskrit: pṛthivīnabhasī cobhe viśrute viśvalaukike tayoḥ saṃdhāraṇārthaṃ hi mām adhokṣajam añjasā
english: The earth and the sky are both renowned, belonging to the whole world; and for the upholding of these two, I am rightly called Adhokṣaja.

sanskrit: niruktaṃ vedaviduṣo ye ca śabdārthacintakāḥ te māṃ gāyanti prāgvaṃśe adhokṣaja iti sthitiḥ
english: Those learned in the Veda and those who ponder the meaning of words sing of me by this etymology in the eastern sacrificial hall: "Adhokṣaja" is the established name.

sanskrit: śabda ekamatair eṣa vyāhṛtaḥ paramarṣibhiḥ nānyo hy adhokṣajo loke ṛte nārāyaṇaṃ prabhum
english: This word has been uttered with one accord by the supreme sages; for there is in the world no other Adhokṣaja than the lord Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: ghṛtaṃ mamārciṣo loke jantūnāṃ prāṇadhāraṇam ghṛtārcir aham avyagrair vedajñaiḥ parikīrtitaḥ
english: The ghee of my flames in the world is the sustenance of the breath of creatures; I am proclaimed Ghṛtārcis, the ghee-flamed, by the untroubled knowers of the Veda.

sanskrit: trayo hi dhātavaḥ khyātāḥ karmajā iti ca smṛtāḥ pittaṃ śleṣmā ca vāyuś ca eṣa saṃghāta ucyate
english: Three humours are declared, and they are remembered as born of action: bile, phlegm, and wind; this is called their combination.

sanskrit: etaiś ca dhāryate jantur etaiḥ kṣīṇaiś ca kṣīyate āyurvedavidas tasmāt tridhātuṃ māṃ pracakṣate
english: By these the creature is sustained, and when these decay it decays; therefore those versed in the science of life declare me to be the threefold humour.

sanskrit: vṛṣo hi bhagavān dharmaḥ khyāto lokeṣu bhārata naighaṇṭukapadākhyātaṃ viddhi māṃ vṛṣam uttamam
english: The blessed Dharma is renowned in the worlds as the Bull, O Bhārata; know me as the supreme Bull, declared by the word of the lexicon.

sanskrit: kapir varāhaḥ śreṣṭhaś ca dharmaś ca vṛṣa ucyate tasmād vṛṣākapiṃ prāha kaśyapo māṃ prajāpatiḥ
english: Kapi is the boar, the best, and dharma is called the Bull; therefore Kaśyapa the Prajāpati called me Vṛṣākapi.

sanskrit: na cādiṃ na madhyaṃ tathā naiva cāntaṃ; kadā cid vidante surāś cāsurāś ca anādyo hy amadhyas tathā cāpy anantaḥ; pragīto 'ham īśo vibhur lokasākṣī
english: Neither my beginning nor my middle, nor yet my end, do gods and demons ever know; for, without beginning, without middle, and likewise without end, I am hymned as the Lord, the all-pervading, the witness of the worlds.

sanskrit: śucīni śravaṇīyāni śṛṇomīha dhanaṃjaya na ca pāpāni gṛhṇāmi tato 'haṃ vai śuciśravāḥ
english: Pure things, worthy to be heard, do I hear here, O Dhanaṃjaya, and I take no heed of sinful things; therefore am I Śuciśravas, of pure renown.
